## Wednesday: Highlights

- File paths: local (irreproducible) vs URL (reproducible)

### Irreproducible: "C:/Users/.../data.csv"

### Preferred: "https://uofi.box.com/shared/static/data.csv"

- File extensions can be helpful but are not necessarily aligned

- Open the file and check the structure for yourself

## Wednesday: Highlights

- Structured data

  - Rectangular
  - Rows and columns
  - Delimiter such as `, |&.;`

## Wednesday: Highlights

- Delimiter is comma

```{r echo=TRUE}
# comma delimited
readr::read_csv("https://uofi.box.com/shared/static/sctl0dsd72wubxfrn7ko0v6namn9fhl4.csv") |>
  head(3) |>
  print(width = Inf)
```

## Wednesday: Highlights

- Delimiter is tab

```{r echo=TRUE}
# tab delimited. specify the delimiter via delim =
readr::read_delim("https://uofi.box.com/shared/static/5nqg2dk8uym5u87s9rv1gq10mtxnybij.txt", delim = "\t") |>
  head(3) |>
  print(width = Inf)
```

## Wednesday: Highlights

- Semi-structured data

  - Human-readable text with keystroke separators such as `[] : , ""`\
  - JSON, geoJSON, html, xml

```{r echo=TRUE}
music_data <- jsonlite::fromJSON("https://uofi.box.com/shared/static/omj8z0gb2zivcuhn5fhqt0n8ahvxwes4.json")

head(music_data$billboard_artist)
```

## Wednesday: Highlights

- Semi-structured data can be deeply nested

```{r echo=TRUE}
unlist(music_data$spotify_data[[1]][[1]][[1]]$name)
```

## Friday: Messy Data Defined

- Reasonably large

- Errors present and frequent

- Inconsistent values

- Improperly formatted column(s)

- Difficult to parse character-valued column(s); not categorical

## Friday: Clean Data Defined

- No errors

- Consistent

- Properly formatted column(s)

- Easily parsed character-valued column(s)

- Ready for analysis

### What we do in this class is transform messy data into clean data.

## Friday: Base R Reminders

- R's strength is **vectorization**.

- Data frames are lists. Lists are not data frames.

- `$` when data frame has names. `[[]]` otherwise.

- `lapply()` for vectorizing on lists.

  - 

    ### Data frames are lists.

## Friday: Using Google Drive as Cloud Storage for Loading Data

- Share as "Anyone with the link"

```         
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Ex8g9--iHoh8A_rPLUcqpUslDVXCWpUW/view?usp=sharing
```

- Locate file ID which is between `/d/` and `/view?usp=sharing` in the URL

```         
1Ex8g9--iHoh8A_rPLUcqpUslDVXCWpUW
```

- Change the URL replacing `/file/d/` with `/uc?export=download&id=` and removing `/view?usp=sharing`

```         
https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1Ex8g9--iHoh8A_rPLUcqpUslDVXCWpUW
```

## Friday: In-class Assignment

A series of timed data science tasks to check your base R knowledge and skills.

*See next slide for 7 problems.*

## Friday: In-class Assignment {.scrollable}

1. Find a JSON data file online and load it into R using either the local download or the URL. (5 minutes)

2. Print the column names of the data frame. (2 minutes)

3. Print the first 10 rows of the data frame such that all columns are visible. (2 minutes)

4. Print the mode, i.e. `mode()`, of each column of the data frame. (1 minute)

5. Print the typeof, i.e. `typeof()`, or class, i.e. `class()`, of each column of the data frame. (1 minute)

6. Pick one column that is character-valued and truncate the character strings to retain only the first 2 characters. (3 minutes)

7. Create a new numeric column representing the number of characters (character length) of one character-valued column. (3 minutes)
